synonyms: Clematis dioica var. drummondii (Torr. & A.Gray) Kuntze
look_here_first: FIRST find the slender open starburst of four pale SEPALS (no true petals) and numerous exposed stamens; purple/scarlet leatherflowers instead hang as leathery urns. Notice opposite compound often deeply LOBED leaflets and a twisting LEAF STALK that clasps supports. Male and female flowers occur on separate vines; only female vines produce the famous shaggy long (4–9 cm) silky style/beak heads. Avoid confusing an introduced white sweet autumn clematis with smooth-edged leaflets and massive bisexual bloom sprays.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Purola natural flora; Travis — UT PRC herbarium specimens; Williamson — UT PRC county field treatment.

best_field_traits: opposite odd-pinnate leaves usually 5-foliolate and deeply divided
four thin white-to-cream sepals spread flat
achenes with extremely long 4–9 cm plumose beaks
morphology_keys.habit: Woody scrambling/climbing vine, often several meters.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Usually odd-pinnate and 5-foliolate; leaflets often deeply divided or cleft.
morphology_keys.flower: Open rather than urn-shaped; four thin white/cream spreading sepals; male and female flowers on separate vines.
morphology_keys.fruit: Aggregate achenes with very long silky plumose beaks forming conspicuous 'old man's beard' masses.
morphology_keys.family_backfill_note: Ranunculaceae family backfill uses C. drummondii as the open-flower Clematis anchor: petaloid sepals + many free stamens/pistils + aggregate achenes.

comparisons.key_distinctions: C. terniflora has masses of small bisexual white flowers and mostly entire 3–5-foliolate leaves. C. pitcheri has thick purple urn-shaped flowers.
